summary: TLS session ticket rotation causing burst 5xx and streaming handshake thrash in us-east-prod
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC, NimbusAI reported elevated 5xx rates across streaming and short-payload requests in us-east (prod). Root cause appears correlated with TLS session ticket rotation events on the edge LB, which trigger mass upstream reconnections and a transient spike in runtime handshake CPU and connection failures. Impact: ~12% increased 5xx rate for affected tenant across streaming and sync calls for ~2 minutes every 15 minutes. Several streaming sessions were dropped and customers reported higher latency and reconnect loops.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbusAI tenant credentials against prod endpoint in us-east with streaming chat session (keep-alive enabled)
2) Observe successful streams for ~13 minutes, then at the next TLS ticket rotation window several streams drop and subsequent requests return 502/503/524 depending on path
3) Reproduce by forcing TLS ticket rotation on edge LB (internal staging test) and concurrently generate small sync requests and long-lived streams
logs: Edge LB logs show TLS ticket-rotation event at 02:15:00 UTC with a spike of TCP CLOSE_WAIT and new TLS handshakes. Apigw proxy metrics: connection resets +380% and backend 5xx increased from baseline 0.6% to 12.4% for the tenant. Serving-runtime logs show handshake timeouts and ephemeral worker CPU spiking to 95% on several pods, followed by connection backpressure and 502s. Sample traces: trace-id 6af3e2b2-prod-331 (stream drop), trace-id 9d72b1a1-prod-338 (sync 502).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: TLS ticket rotation at the edge is causing simultaneous renegotiation that overwhelms connection pool and runtime handshake CPU due to Nagle-disabled small payload traffic pattern. Verified rotation schedule matches incident windows (every 15m). Observed that when rotation occurs, upstream keepalive sockets close; apigw does immediate reconnect fanout to serving-runtime which triggers brief connection storm. Autoscaler does not react within the 2-minute window; pods transiently hit accept-queue limits leading to 502/503 responses. Related internal ticket INT-4802 contains prior notes on connection pool tuning. Miguel Ortega (SRE) reproduced on staging by replaying traffic and forcing ticket rotation; Linh Tran (runtime) observed ephemeral OOM in a debug pod when handshake backlog exceeded 512.
workaround: 1) Temporary mitigation: Disable aggressive TLS ticket rotation on edge for NimbusAI via config toggle (set rotation interval to 24h) — applied 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC. 2) Route NimbusAI tenant to a warmed pool of runtime instances with increased accept-queue and keepalive window until proper fix. These reduced 5xx spike amplitude to ~1.1%.
resolution: Mitigation in place reduces customer impact. Recommended permanent fixes: adjust edge LB ticket rotation to be rolling (staggered across nodes) and implement connection backoff at apigw to avoid immediate fanout reacquisitions. Runtime team to add handshake rate-limiting and increase default accept-queue for streaming-heavy tenants. Follow-up tasks created: INT-4929 (edge rolling rotation rollout), INT-4930 (apigw backoff).
next_steps:
- SRE to implement rolling ticket rotation by 2026-03-15 (INT-4929).
- Runtime to add handshake rate limiter and monitor acceptance queue over next deploy (INT-4930).
- CS to inform NimbusAI of mitigation and timeline; schedule 1:1 on 2026-03-13.
- Postmortem to be drafted after full deployment of fixes.
